346	    def _route_cells(self, exclude_id: str) -> set[Position]:
347	        """Cells every robot except *exclude_id* still plans to drive through."""
348	        cells: set[Position] = set()
349	        for robot in self.robots.values():
350	            if robot.robot_id != exclude_id:
351	                cells.update(robot.route)
352	        return cells
353	
354	    def _idle_sidestep_cell(
355	        self,
356	        blocker: Robot,
357	        requester: Robot,
358	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
359	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
360	    ) -> Position | None:
361	        """Free side-cell an idle blocker can yield to, or None.
362	
363	        The target may not be the requester's own cell (that would swap the
364	        two robots within one tick) nor any cell another robot still plans to
365	        drive through, so the blocker never trades one blockage for another.
366	        """
367	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=blocker.robot_id)
368	        for cell in self.grid.neighbors(blocker.position):
369	            if cell == requester.position:
370	                continue
371	            if cell in occupied or cell in reserved:
372	                continue
373	            if cell in on_routes:
374	                continue
375	            return cell
376	        return None
377	
378	    def _self_sidestep(
379	        self,
380	        robot: Robot,
381	        task: Task | None,
382	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
383	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
384	        already_moved: frozenset[str] = frozenset(),
385	    ) -> tuple[Position, list[Position]] | None:
386	        """Best side cell plus replanned route for a blocked robot, or None.
387	
388	        Only cells off every other robot's planned route qualify, and only if
389	        the task remains reachable from there. A candidate that merely retreats
390	        along the corridor only to face the very same blocker again on the next
391	        tick is rejected too: such a move records mileage and gets undone
392	        forever instead of making progress, even when more empty cells stretch
393	        out behind the robot. Candidates are ranked by replanned route length
394	        with the deterministic neighbor order (up, left, right, down) breaking
395	        ties. *already_moved* names robots that have used their one move of
396	        this tick and therefore cannot vacate a cell to resolve the block.
397	        """
398	        if task is None or task.completed:
399	            return None
400	        destination = robot.route[0]
401	        blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
402	        if blocker_id is None:
403	            blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
404	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=robot.robot_id)
405	        best: tuple[int, int, Position, list[Position]] | None = None
406	        for index, cell in enumerate(self.grid.neighbors(robot.position)):
407	            if cell in occupied or cell in reserved or cell in on_routes:
408	                continue
409	            route = self._plan_route(robot, task, start=cell)
410	            if route is None:
411	                continue
412	            if (
413	                blocker_id is not None
414	                and blocker_id != robot.robot_id
415	                and self._is_bounceback_retreat(
416	                    robot, cell, route, blocker_id, occupied, reserved, already_moved
417	                )
418	            ):
419	                # The replanned route immediately returns through the cell the
420	                # robot is vacating and the blocker cannot use that opening to
421	                # leave: the move would be undone on the next tick.
422	                continue
423	            if best is None or (len(route), index) < (best[0], best[1]):
424	                best = (len(route), index, cell, route)
425	        if best is None:
426	            return None
427	        return best[2], best[3]

429	    def _is_bounceback_retreat(
430	        self,
431	        robot: Robot,
432	        side: Position,
433	        replanned: Sequence[Position],
434	        blocker_id: str,
435	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
436	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
437	        already_moved: frozenset[str],
438	    ) -> bool:
439	        """Whether stepping to *side* only sends the robot back to the block.
440	
441	        A retreat is futile when the replanned route leads straight back through
442	        the robot's current cell and still runs through the blocker's cell (so
443	        the side move is undone next tick with the same blocker ahead) while
444	        the blocker cannot leave its own cell through the gap that opens up.
445	        A route that bypasses the blocker entirely is a genuine detour and is
446	        never rejected here.
447	        """
448	        if not replanned or replanned[0] != robot.position:
449	            return False
450	        blocker = self.robots.get(blocker_id)
451	        if blocker is None or blocker.position not in replanned:
452	            return False
453	        # Hypothetical end-of-tick layout: the requester has vacated its cell
454	        # and stands on the candidate side cell.
455	        hyp_occupied = dict(occupied)
456	        del hyp_occupied[robot.position]
457	        hyp_occupied[side] = robot.robot_id
458	        # The requester only gets back onto its route by driving through these
459	        # cells, so a blocker may only "leave" by driving on, never by parking
460	        # on the replanned route. The requester cannot make a second move
461	        # within this tick, and neither can a robot that already moved.
462	        blocked_path = frozenset(replanned)
463	        return not self._can_vacate(
464	            blocker,
465	            robot,
466	            hyp_occupied,
467	            reserved,
468	            frozenset({robot.robot_id}) | already_moved,
469	            blocked_path,
470	        )
471	
472	    def _can_vacate(
473	        self,
474	        blocker: Robot,
475	        requester: Robot,
476	        occupied: dict[Position, str],
477	        reserved: dict[Position, str],
478	        checking: frozenset[str],
479	        blocked_path: frozenset[Position],
480	    ) -> bool:
481	        """Whether *blocker* can leave its cell this tick in the given layout.
482	
483	        An idle blocker leaves only by yielding onto a safe side cell for the
484	        requesting robot; a busy blocker leaves by driving onto its next
485	        waypoint (possibly following a chain of robots that all move this tick)
486	        or by sidestepping onto a free adjacent cell itself. Robots paused by
487	        map unreachability never move. *checking* names robots whose leave
488	        check is already on the call stack, so a cyclic dependency (a head-on
489	        deadlock, or the requester itself) is not assumed resolvable.
490	        *blocked_path* holds the cells the retreating requester must drive back
491	        through: another robot parking there only moves the blockage, so such
492	        sidesteps do not count as leaving (driving on along the cell on the
493	        blocker's own route does).
494	        """
495	        if blocker.robot_id in checking:
496	            return False
497	        task = self.tasks[blocker.task_id] if blocker.task_id is not None else None
498	        if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
499	            return False
500	        if task is not None and not blocker.route:
501	            # A busy robot with no route left only arrives/finishes this tick;
502	            # it never drives or sidesteps for anyone.
503	            return False
504	        if task is None:
505	            # Idle robots only ever move by yielding for a requester.
506	            side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, requester, occupied, reserved)
507	            return side is not None and side not in blocked_path
508	        if blocker.route:
509	            ahead = blocker.route[0]
510	            if (
511	                self.grid.traversable(ahead)
512	                and ahead not in occupied
513	                and ahead not in reserved
514	            ):
515	                return True
516	            occupant_id = occupied.get(ahead) or reserved.get(ahead)
517	            if (
518	                occupant_id is not None
519	                and occupant_id != blocker.robot_id
520	                and occupant_id not in checking
521	            ):
522	                # The blocker could follow the robot ahead once that robot
523	                # vacates its cell this same tick.
524	                if self._can_vacate(
525	                    self.robots[occupant_id],
526	                    requester,
527	                    occupied,
528	                    reserved,
529	                    checking | {blocker.robot_id},
530	                    blocked_path,
531	                ):
532	                    return True
533	        # Otherwise the blocker might sidestep onto a free side cell itself,
534	        # but not onto a cell the retreating requester still has to use.
535	        on_routes = self._route_cells(exclude_id=blocker.robot_id)
536	        for side_cell in self.grid.neighbors(blocker.position):
537	            if (
538	                side_cell in occupied
539	                or side_cell in reserved
540	                or side_cell in on_routes
541	                or side_cell in blocked_path
542	            ):
543	                continue
544	            if self._plan_route(blocker, task, start=side_cell) is not None:
545	                return True
546	        return False
547	
548	    def _update_traffic_waits(
549	        self,
550	        waited: dict[str, str],
551	        moved_ids: frozenset[str],
552	    ) -> None:
553	        """Keep only waits that still hold once the tick's moves have settled.
554	
555	        *waited* maps every robot that stopped this tick purely because
556	        another robot held its next waypoint to the robot it saw there at the
557	        time; *moved_ids* names the robots that ended up moving. The mid-tick
558	        impression is not trusted on its own, because the blocker may itself
559	        drive on (or make room for yet another robot) later in the same tick.
560	        A record survives only when the robot neither moved nor paused and its
561	        next waypoint is occupied by another robot in the final layout; the
562	        reported blocker is whichever robot actually occupies that cell. Any
563	        other outcome -- the robot moved, its task paused, or the way ahead
564	        cleared -- deletes the entry. A wait that continues without a free tick
565	        in between keeps accumulating even when the blocker changes identity;
566	        once interrupted, a later blockage starts a fresh count at one.
567	        """
568	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
569	        surviving: dict[str, dict[str, object]] = {}
570	        for robot_id in waited:
571	            if robot_id in moved_ids:
572	                continue
573	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
574	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
575	                continue
576	            task = self.tasks.get(robot.task_id) if robot.task_id is not None else None
577	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
578	                continue
579	            blocker_id = occupied.get(robot.route[0])
580	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot_id:
581	                continue
582	            entry = self._traffic_waits.get(robot_id)
583	            if entry is None:
584	                surviving[robot_id] = {"blocked_by": [blocker_id], "ticks": 1}
585	            else:
586	                surviving[robot_id] = {
587	                    "blocked_by": [blocker_id],
588	                    "ticks": int(entry["ticks"]) + 1,
589	                }
590	        self._traffic_waits = surviving
591	
592	    def _reconcile_traffic_waits_after_map_change(self) -> None:
593	        """Drop wait records an accepted map edit has invalidated.
594	
595	        A map change never moves a robot, so it can neither create a wait nor
596	        add to one; but it can end one. A robot whose task just paused on
597	        unreachability has no route left to wait on, and a robot whose
598	        replanned next cell is no longer held by the recorded blocker is not
599	        blocked by it anymore -- both records are removed. An entry whose
600	        robot still faces the very same blocker on its refreshed route keeps
601	        its count untouched, whatever else the edit changed.
602	        """
603	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
604	        for robot_id, entry in list(self._traffic_waits.items()):
605	            robot = self.robots.get(robot_id)
606	            if robot is None or not robot.route:
607	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
608	                continue
609	            if occupied.get(robot.route[0]) not in entry["blocked_by"]:
610	                del self._traffic_waits[robot_id]
611	
612	    def _traffic_wait_report(self) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
613	        return [
614	            {
615	                "robot_id": robot_id,
616	                "blocked_by": list(entry["blocked_by"]),
617	                "ticks": entry["ticks"],
618	            }
619	            for robot_id, entry in sorted(self._traffic_waits.items())
620	        ]

626	    def assign_tasks(self) -> None:
627	        """Assign pending tasks to the nearest idle robot using stable tie breaks."""
628	        pending = [task for task in self.tasks.values() if task.assigned_robot is None]
629	        for task in sorted(pending, key=lambda item: item.task_id):
630	            choices: list[tuple[int, str, list[tuple[int, int]]]] = []
631	            for robot in self.robots.values():
632	                if not robot.idle:
633	                    continue
634	                try:
635	                    route = shortest_path(self.grid, robot.position, task.pickup)
636	                    route += shortest_path(self.grid, task.pickup, task.dropoff)
637	                except ValueError:
638	                    continue
639	                choices.append((len(route), robot.robot_id, route))
640	            if not choices:
641	                # No robot can reach this task yet; it keeps waiting and does
642	                # not block assignment of other tasks.
643	                continue
644	            _, robot_id, route = min(choices)
645	            robot = self.robots[robot_id]
646	            robot.task_id = task.task_id
647	            robot.route = route
648	            task.assigned_robot = robot_id
649	
650	    def _confirm_pickups(self) -> None:
651	        """A robot starting a tick on its pickup point collects first."""
652	        for robot in self.robots.values():
653	            if robot.task_id is None:
654	                continue
655	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
656	            if not task.completed and not task.picked_up and robot.position == task.pickup:
657	                task.picked_up = True
658	
659	    def step(self) -> dict[str, object]:
660	        self._confirm_pickups()
661	        self._recover_paused_tasks()
662	        self.assign_tasks()
663	        # A robot assigned while already standing on the pickup cell collects
664	        # immediately instead of driving off without the goods.
665	        self._confirm_pickups()
666	        occupied = {robot.position: robot.robot_id for robot in self.robots.values()}
667	        reserved: dict[tuple[int, int], str] = {}
668	        moved: list[str] = []
669	        moved_ids: set[str] = set()
670	        blocked_by: dict[str, str] = {}
671	
672	        def relocate(robot: Robot, destination: tuple[int, int]) -> None:
673	            del occupied[robot.position]
674	            robot.position = destination
675	            robot.distance_travelled += 1
676	            occupied[destination] = robot.robot_id
677	            reserved[destination] = robot.robot_id
678	            moved.append(robot.robot_id)
679	            moved_ids.add(robot.robot_id)
680	
681	        for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id):
682	            if robot.robot_id in moved_ids:
683	                # Already yielded this tick at another robot's request.
684	                continue
685	            task = self.tasks[robot.task_id] if robot.task_id is not None else None
686	            if task is not None and task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
687	                # Paused by map unreachability: stays put, never yields.
688	                continue
689	            if not robot.route:
690	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
691	                continue
692	            destination = robot.route[0]
693	            if not self.grid.traversable(destination):
694	                # Defensive: routes are normally replanned on every map edit.
695	                if task is not None and not task.completed:
696	                    route = self._plan_route(robot, task)
697	                    if route is None:
698	                        robot.route = []
699	                        self.paused_tasks.add(task.task_id)
700	                    else:
701	                        robot.route = route
702	                continue
703	            blocker_id = occupied.get(destination)
704	            if blocker_id is None:
705	                blocker_id = reserved.get(destination)
706	            if blocker_id is None or blocker_id == robot.robot_id:
707	                relocate(robot, destination)
708	                robot.route.pop(0)
709	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
710	                continue
711	            # Another robot is in the way; this is distinct from a
712	            # map-unreachability pause and the task stays active.
713	            blocker = self.robots[blocker_id]
714	            if blocker_id not in moved_ids:
715	                if blocker.task_id is None:
716	                    # Idle blocker: ask it to yield onto a free side cell,
717	                    # then take over the cell it vacated.
718	                    side = self._idle_sidestep_cell(blocker, robot, occupied, reserved)
719	                    if side is not None:
720	                        relocate(blocker, side)
721	                        relocate(robot, destination)
722	                        robot.route.pop(0)
723	                        self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
724	                        continue
725	                elif blocker.route:
726	                    ahead = blocker.route[0]
727	                    if (
728	                        self.grid.traversable(ahead)
729	                        and ahead not in occupied
730	                        and ahead not in reserved
731	                    ):
732	                        # The blocker is expected to drive on within this
733	                        # tick, so waiting one tick is cheaper than detouring.
734	                        blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
735	                        continue
736	            # The blocker cannot or will not move this tick: try to sidestep
737	            # onto a free adjacent cell and replan from there.
738	            side = self._self_sidestep(
739	                robot, task, occupied, reserved, frozenset(moved_ids)
740	            )
741	            if side is not None:
742	                cell, route = side
743	                relocate(robot, cell)
744	                robot.route = route
745	                self._finish_if_arrived(robot)
746	                continue
747	            blocked_by[robot.robot_id] = blocker_id
748	        self._update_traffic_waits(blocked_by, frozenset(moved_ids))
749	        self.tick += 1
750	        event: dict[str, object] = {
751	            "type": "tick",
752	            "tick": self.tick,
753	            "moved": moved,
754	            "robots": {robot_id: list(robot.position) for robot_id, robot in sorted(self.robots.items())},
755	            "completed": sorted(task.task_id for task in self.tasks.values() if task.completed),
756	        }
757	        self.replay.append(event)
758	        return event
759	
760	    def _finish_if_arrived(self, robot: Robot) -> None:
761	        if robot.task_id is None:
762	            return
763	        task = self.tasks[robot.task_id]
764	        if task.task_id in self.paused_tasks:
765	            return
766	        if robot.position == task.pickup:
767	            task.picked_up = True
768	        if task.picked_up and robot.position == task.dropoff and not robot.route:
769	            task.completed = True
770	            self.paused_tasks.discard(task.task_id)
771	            robot.task_id = None
772

774	        completed = sum(task.completed for task in self.tasks.values())
775	        return {
776	            "ticks": self.tick,
777	            "tasks_total": len(self.tasks),
778	            "tasks_completed": completed,
779	            "tasks_paused": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
780	            "completion_ratio": completed / len(self.tasks) if self.tasks else 1.0,
781	            "distance_total": sum(robot.distance_travelled for robot in self.robots.values()),
782	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
783	        }

813	    def save_checkpoint(self, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> None:
814	        """Write the simulator state to *path* without changing this instance.
815	
816	        The write is atomic: an existing destination keeps either its complete
817	        old contents or the complete new contents, and a brand-new destination
818	        is either fully created or left absent. Filesystem or permission errors
819	        raise :class:`OSError`.
820	        """
821	        document = {
822	            "version": CHECKPOINT_VERSION,
823	            "grid": {
824	                "width": self.grid.width,
825	                "height": self.grid.height,
826	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.grid.obstacles)],
827	            },
828	            "base_grid": {
829	                "width": self.base_grid.width,
830	                "height": self.base_grid.height,
831	                "obstacles": [list(cell) for cell in sorted(self.base_grid.obstacles)],
832	            },
833	            "tick": self.tick,
834	            "robots": [
835	                {
836	                    "robot_id": robot.robot_id,
837	                    "position": list(robot.position),
838	                    "route": [list(cell) for cell in robot.route],
839	                    "task_id": robot.task_id,
840	                    "distance_travelled": robot.distance_travelled,
841	                }
842	                for robot in sorted(self.robots.values(), key=lambda item: item.robot_id)
843	            ],
844	            "tasks": [
845	                {
846	                    "task_id": task.task_id,
847	                    "pickup": list(task.pickup),
848	                    "dropoff": list(task.dropoff),
849	                    "assigned_robot": task.assigned_robot,
850	                    "picked_up": task.picked_up,
851	                    "completed": task.completed,
852	                }
853	                for task in sorted(self.tasks.values(), key=lambda item: item.task_id)
854	            ],
855	            "replay": copy.deepcopy(self.replay),
856	            "map_changes": copy.deepcopy(self.map_changes),
857	            "paused_tasks": sorted(self.paused_tasks),
858	            "traffic_waits": self._traffic_wait_report(),
859	        }
860	        payload = (json.dumps(document, ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, indent=2) + "\n").encode("utf-8")
861	
862	        directory = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(os.fspath(path))) or os.curdir
863	        fd, tmp_name = tempfile.mkstemp(prefix=".checkpoint-", suffix=".tmp", dir=directory)
864	        try:
865	            handle = os.fdopen(fd, "wb")
866	            try:
867	                handle.write(payload)
868	                handle.flush()
869	                os.fsync(handle.fileno())
870	            finally:
871	                handle.close()
872	            os.replace(tmp_name, path)
873	            self._fsync_directory(directory)
874	        except BaseException:
875	            # After a successful replace the temp name is already gone.
876	            try:
877	                os.unlink(tmp_name)
878	            except OSError:
879	                pass
880	            raise
881	
882	    @staticmethod
883	    def _fsync_directory(directory: str) -> None:
884	        try:
885	            dir_fd = os.open(directory, os.O_RDONLY)
886	        except OSError:
887	            return
888	        try:
889	            os.fsync(dir_fd)
890	        except OSError:
891	            pass
892	        finally:
893	            os.close(dir_fd)

895	    @classmethod
896	    def load_checkpoint(cls, path: str | os.PathLike[str]) -> FleetSimulator:
897	        """Load an independent simulator instance from *path*.
898	
899	        The returned simulator shares no mutable state with the file or any
900	        other loaded instance. Invalid checkpoint content raises
901	        :class:`ValueError` explaining the reason; read/permission failures
902	        propagate as :class:`OSError`.
903	        """
904	        try:
905	            with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
906	                text = handle.read()
907	        except OSError:
908	            raise
909	        try:
910	            data = json.loads(text)
911	        except json.JSONDecodeError as exc:
912	            raise ValueError(f"checkpoint is not valid JSON: {exc.msg}") from exc
913	        return cls._from_checkpoint(data)
914	
915	    @classmethod
916	    def _from_checkpoint(cls, data: object) -> FleetSimulator:
917	        if not isinstance(data, dict):
918	            raise ValueError("checkpoint root must be a JSON object")
919	
920	        version = data.get("version")
921	        if not _is_int(version):
922	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'version' must be an integer")
923	        if version not in _SUPPORTED_VERSIONS:
924	            raise ValueError(
925	                f"unsupported checkpoint version {version}; supported versions: "
926	                f"{sorted(_SUPPORTED_VERSIONS)}"
927	            )
928	
929	        grid = cls._load_grid(data)
930	        tick = cls._load_tick(data)
931	        robot_records, task_records = cls._load_entities(data)
932	
933	        map_changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
934	        paused: set[str] = set()
935	        if version == 1:
936	            replay = cls._load_legacy_replay(data)
937	            base_grid = grid
938	        else:
939	            replay = cls._load_replay(data)
940	            map_changes = cls._load_map_changes(data)
941	            paused = cls._load_paused_tasks(data)
942	            base_grid = cls._load_base_grid(data)

1208	    @classmethod
1209	    def _load_map_changes(cls, data: Mapping[str, object]) -> list[dict[str, object]]:
1210	        raw = cls._require_field(data, "map_changes")
1211	        if not isinstance(raw, list):
1212	            raise ValueError("checkpoint field 'map_changes' must be a list")
1213	        changes: list[dict[str, object]] = []
1214	        last_tick = -1
1215	        last_sequence = 0
1216	        for index, frame in enumerate(raw):
1217	            context = f"map change {index}"
1218	            if not isinstance(frame, dict):
1219	                raise ValueError(f"{context} must be an object")
1220	            tick = frame.get("tick")
1221	            sequence = frame.get("sequence")
1222	            if not _is_int(tick) or tick < 0:
1223	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'tick' must be a non-negative integer")
1224	            if not _is_int(sequence) or sequence <= 0:
1225	                raise ValueError(f"{context} field 'sequence' must be a positive integer")
1226	            if sequence != index + 1:
1227	                raise ValueError(
1228	                    f"map change sequences must run consecutively from 1; change {index} "
1229	                    f"has sequence {sequence}, expected {index + 1}"
1230	                )
1231	            if tick < last_tick:
1232	                raise ValueError(
1233	                    f"{context} tick {tick} is earlier than a preceding map change"
1234	                )
1235	            if tick == last_tick and sequence != last_sequence + 1:
1236	                raise ValueError(f"{context} breaks consecutive sequencing at tick {tick}")
1237	            added = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("added"), context, "added")
1238	            removed = cls._load_change_cells(frame.get("removed"), context, "removed")
1239	            if not added and not removed:
1240	                raise ValueError(f"{context} contains no actual obstacle changes")
1241	            overlap = set(added) & set(removed)
1242	            if overlap:
1243	                cell = sorted(overlap)[0]
1244	                raise ValueError(
1245	                    f"{context} adds and removes the same cell {list(cell)}"
1246	                )
1247	            changes.append(
1248	                {
1249	                    "type": "map_change",
1250	                    "tick": tick,
1251	                    "sequence": sequence,
1252	                    "added": [list(cell) for cell in added],
1253	                    "removed": [list(cell) for cell in removed],
1254	                }
1255	            )
1256	            last_tick = tick
1257	            last_sequence = sequence
1258	        return changes

1260	    @classmethod
1261	    def _validate_map_history(
1262	        cls,
1263	        base_grid: GridMap,
1264	        saved_grid: GridMap,
1265	        changes: Sequence[Mapping[str, object]],
1266	    ) -> None:
1267	        obstacles = set(base_grid.obstacles)
1268	        width, height = saved_grid.width, saved_grid.height
1269	        for frame in changes:
1270	            for key in ("added", "removed"):
1271	                for cell in frame[key]:
1272	                    x, y = cell
1273	                    if not (0 <= x < width and 0 <= y < height):
1274	                        raise ValueError(
1275	                            f"map change {frame['sequence']} cell {list(cell)} lies "
1276	                            "outside the map"
1277	                        )
1278	            added = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["added"]}
1279	            removed = {tuple(cell) for cell in frame["removed"]}
1280	            for cell in added:
1281	                if cell in obstacles:
1282	                    raise ValueError(
1283	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} adds obstacle {list(cell)} "
1284	                        "that is already present according to the history"
1285	                    )
1286	            for cell in removed:
1287	                if cell not in obstacles:
1288	                    raise ValueError(
1289	                        f"map change {frame['sequence']} removes obstacle {list(cell)} "
1290	                        "that is absent according to the history"
1291	                    )
1292	            obstacles |= added
1293	            obstacles -= removed
1294	        if obstacles != set(saved_grid.obstacles):
1295	            raise ValueError(
1296	                "the map reproduced from 'map_changes' does not match the saved grid"

1416	    @staticmethod
1417	    def _validate_active_task_routes(
1418	        paused: set[str],
1419	        task_by_id: Mapping[str, Task],
1420	        robot_by_id: Mapping[str, Robot],
1421	    ) -> None:
1422	        """Reject routes that cannot finish the task each robot is bound to.
1423	
1424	        Traversability and adjacency are checked elsewhere. This enforces the
1425	        pickup/delivery business rules for tasks that are assigned, unfinished
1426	        and not paused by map unreachability: a non-empty route must end at the
1427	        dropoff, and a robot that has not collected yet -- and is not already
1428	        standing on the pickup cell -- must still pass through the pickup.
